To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the problem of Topology control with cooperative Communication (TCC), which is a novel model that allows combining partial message to decode a complete one, in ad hoc networks is NIP-complete; 2) we designed two distributed and localized TCC algorithms that use either 1-hop or 2-hop neighborhood knowledge, which can be applied on any symmetric, strongly connected topology to reduce total energy consumption; 3) we analyzed the performance of our algorithms through extensive simulation.
the TCC algorithm is NIP-complete, and that our two algorithms are able to reduce power consumption by up to 30%, compared to the case where nodes use only 1-hop information.
we propose two localized algorithms for topology control in ad hoc networks that use cooperative communications.
